data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Biological evolution has no goal of truth, whereas scientific methodology explicitly aims at verisimilitude.","A courtroom verdict often aims for finality (probability > threshold), whereas Popperian science never accepts a theory as finally verified."],"overturn_conditions":["If it can be shown that past survival correlates with no future resilience even as a matter of fact, the pragmatic basis vanishes.","If the definition of 'severe test' is shown to be circular or theory-laden in a way that biases the outcome."],"shared_structure":["Survival of the fittest theory mirrors survival of the fittest species; neither guarantees future survival, but past survival is the only rational basis for selection.","Cross-examination in court eliminates weak testimonies; the remaining testimony is preferred not because it is certainly true, but because it has resisted the strongest attacks."],"source_memory_refs":["evolutionary-selection-of-species","courtroom-adversarial-testing"],"transfer_claims":["Just as we bet on the species that survived ice ages to colonize a new cold region, we bet on the theory that survived severe tests to guide action.","The rationality of the choice lies in the process of elimination, not in the intrinsic properties of the survivor."]},"claim":"Popper's preference for the better-corroborated theory is defensible on his own terms as a methodological rule for 'verisimilitude-seeking' rather than an inductive probability assignment; it survives by redefining rational action as the strategic selection of the theory with the highest known content and severest testing history, accepting the cost that this preference offers no guarantee of future success or truth, only the best available guess based on past error-elimination.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If corroboration is interpreted as assigning a higher degree of belief or subjective confidence, the defense collapses into hidden induction.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the preference is claimed to minimize the risk of practical failure in a probabilistic sense, it contradicts Popper's denial that survival implies reliability.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the agent cannot articulate the difference between 'best guess' and 'most probable', the distinction is merely verbal.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism distinguishes between 'logical probability' (which Popper rejects as increasing with evidence) and 'methodological preference' (which increases with severity of tests passed). By treating corroboration as a report of past performance in falsification attempts, the scientist chooses the theory that has proven most robust against error, not because it is likely true, but because it is the most informative surviving conjecture. This avoids induction by refusing to project past success into future probability, instead projecting it as a basis for critical discussion and further testing.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
